headline: Record revenue and profit quarter, opex outlook lowered
summary_short: Robinhood's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,308M (+32.3% y/y, +22.6% q/q) on record trading and Gold-subscriber growth, while net income climbed to $561M (+45.3% y/y), including a $129M RVI-deconsolidation gain.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $1,308M (+32.3% y/y, +22.6% q/q), led by transaction-based revenue +44% y/y (event contracts >10x, options +29%, equities +95%, crypto -38%) and other revenue +54% y/y on Trump Accounts and Gold subscriptions. Net income was $561M (+45.3% y/y), including $129M of RVI-deconsolidation gains ($0.14 of the $0.62 diluted EPS). Total opex rose 33% y/y on marketing, a one-time restructuring charge, and Trump Accounts/Rothera costs. Robinhood lowered its FY2026 Adjusted Opex-and-SBC outlook to $2.675-$2.775B, from $2.7-$2.825B at Q1. Cash rose to $5,362M after a $2.2B convertible-notes issuance and $414M of buybacks; equity was $9,541M, down 1.5% q/q, up 18.2% y/y.

drivers.explanation: Transaction-based revenue +44% y/y on event contracts (>10x), options (+29%) and equities (+95%), partly offset by crypto (-38%); net interest +9% on higher interest-earning assets; other revenue +54% on Trump Accounts and Gold subscriptions.
Included $129M of gains primarily from the deconsolidation of Robinhood Ventures Fund I (RVI); underlying growth also reflects revenue outpacing a 33% y/y rise in operating expenses.

Total operating expenses rose 33% y/y on marketing and growth investment, one-time restructuring charges from the June 2026 reduction-in-force, and costs tied to Trump Accounts and Rothera — expense growth trailed revenue growth.
Diluted EPS growth included $0.14 of the RVI-deconsolidation gain (of $0.62 total); diluted share count was roughly flat at 912M vs 909M a year earlier.
Includes net proceeds from Robinhood's June 2026 convertible senior notes offering ($2.2B issued); $414M was used for share repurchases in the quarter, including $290M tied to the notes offering.
not explained in the release — only y/y (not q/q) balance-sheet detail is disclosed, so the quarter-over-quarter decline has no stated cause.

Management frames the quarter as broad-based: 13 business lines now exceed $100M in annualized revenue, led by Robinhood Legend, the Credit Card, Trump Accounts, and Rothera; CEO cites "making everyone an owner" as the strategic focus.
